proposition: Let a_0 = 6, a_1 = 22 and a_n = 8*a_(n-1) + (-15)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 20, a_n = 4*3^n + 2*5^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 20, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 20, n^3 is at least 3*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 20, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 20, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 65 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 20, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
The steps above establish the statement up to 20, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 20.
